subtitle: How a Distant Sea-Fight Opened the Gates of the Great Mughal’s Port

panels.shot: split-frame composition, left half low-angle English ship in surf off Suvali, right half royal Mughal balcony over Agra with Jahangir watching an imagined sea
panels.action: On one side, Thomas Best stands on a windswept deck near Swally, hand on railing, English ships behind him; on the other, Jahangir in rich robes leans on a marble jharokha, looking toward a painted sea on a distant wall.

dialogue.text: In November 1612, English guns roared off Swally while Mughal nobles watched from the shore—and a sea battle neither emperor nor sultan fought decided who might trade at Surat.

i18n.hi: नवंबर १६१२ में सुवाली पर अंग्रेज तोपें गरजीं, मुगल अमीर किनारे से देखते रहे — न किसी बादशाह, न किसी सुलतान ने, पर एक समुंदरी लड़ाई ने तय किया किसे सूरत में सौदा मिलेगा।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the Gujarat coast, with Surat in the distance and Swally anchorage in the foreground
panels.action: The Gujarat shoreline stretches under a hazy sky; small craft move on the Tapti near Surat, while in the offing a few tall-masted English ships ride at anchor off the low sandy strip of Suvali.

dialogue.text: Surat, jewel of the Arabian Sea, fed the Mughal treasury with customs and pilgrim ships. Yet its sea-gate, the Swally anchorage at Suvali, was watched by Portuguese cannon at sea and Mughal eyes on land.

i18n.hi: सूरत, अरब सागर का नगीना, महसूल और हज जहाज़ों से मुगल खजाना भरता था। पर उसका समुंदरी फाटक सुवाली की लंगरगाह थी — समंदर में पुर्तगाली तोपें, किनारे पर मुगल निगाहें।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Mughal customs office overlooking the river, with officials examining papers and watching the water
panels.action: Bearded Mughal officials in turbans and layered cotton robes sit on low cushions in a riverfront office, ledgers open, as one clerk pauses, gaze turned toward the distant masts at sea.

dialogue.text: Mughal governors at Surat weighed each foreign flag. The Portuguese Estado da Índia claimed old rights over these waters, yet English factors pressed new petitions for a share of the port’s rich trade.

i18n.hi: सूरत के मुगल सूबेदार हर परायी झंडे को तौलते थे। पुर्तगाली इस्तादो दा इंदिया इन पानी पर पुराने हक जताते, पर अंग्रेज फैक्टर नई अर्ज़ियाँ लेकर बंदर से हिस्से की ज़िद करते।

panels.shot: interior court shot in Agra, Jahangir seated in durbar with nobles, a small painted map of the western coast on a carpet
panels.action: Jahangir sits cross-legged on a jewel-studded throne in a pillared hall, nobles ranked before him; a courtier holds up a painted parchment showing the Gujarat coast and the port of Surat marked in bright color.

dialogue.text: In Agra, Jahangir noted such matters in his Tuzuk with a ruler’s calm pride. Surat’s revenues and pilgrim traffic, he knew, linked his empire to Mecca, Persia and the shores beyond.

i18n.hi: आगरा में जहांगीर ने ऐसे मामलों को तुज़ुक में बादशाही सुकून से लिखा। उसे पता था, सूरत की आमदनी और हाजी जहाज़ उसके मुल्क को मक्का, फ़ारस और दूर के किनारों से जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot on the deck of an English ship at Swally, low-angle on Thomas Best looking toward the land
panels.action: Thomas Best stands on the quarterdeck of a sturdy English ship, sea-wind tugging his cloak, eyes narrowed toward the hazy line of the Gujarat coast where small figures move on the beach.

dialogue.text: In November 1612, Captain Thomas Best of the East India Company anchored off Suvali. His ships carried cloth and hopes, but also guns—aware that Portuguese galleons might contest his very presence.

i18n.hi: नवंबर १६१२ में ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के कप्तान थॉमस बेस्ट ने सुवाली के सामने लंगर डाला। जहाज़ों में कपड़ा था, अरमान थे और तोपें भी — कि कहीं पुर्तगाली गैलियन उनकी मौजूदगी ही परखने न आ जाएं।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Best leaning over a chart table in his cabin, candlelight, charts of the Gulf of Cambay
panels.action: In a timber-beamed cabin lit by a swaying lamp, Thomas Best bends over sea charts of the Gujarat coast, compass in hand, as another officer points to the marked channel toward Swally.

dialogue.speaker: Thomas Best & Jahangir at Swally
dialogue.text: We lie not for adventure, but for Surat. The sea must be held, or all is lost.

i18n.hi: हम रोमांच के लिए नहीं, सूरत के लिए पड़े हैं। ये समंदर थामा तो सब बचा, नहीं तो सब गया।

panels.shot: shoreline wide shot from the Mughal side, with nobles on horseback and elephants watching the distant English ships
panels.action: On the sandy shore near Suvali, Mughal horsemen and attendants cluster around a shaded palanquin; an elephant stands nearby, while all eyes look seaward at the faint shapes of English ships.

dialogue.text: On land, Mughal officials and guards rode down to watch. The empire had no great fleet there; its power walked on land. At Swally, the Mughals would be arbiters, not combatants.

i18n.hi: धरती पर मुगल अमले और सिपाही घोड़ों पर बैठ तमाशा देखने उतर आए। वहां समंदर पर कोई बड़ी मुगल बेड़ा न था; उनकी ताकत ज़मीन पर चलती थी। सुवाली में वे लड़ाके नहीं, पंच बने थे।

panels.shot: dramatic wide sea shot, Portuguese galleons appearing over the horizon under full sail, seen from English deck
panels.action: From the English deck, sailors point as bulky, high-sided Portuguese galleons with crosses on their sails loom over the horizon, lines of smaller craft trailing behind them on the glittering water.

dialogue.text: Soon, Portuguese sails rose from the south. Their Estado claimed to guard the sea-lanes to Surat and the pilgrim ships to Jiddah; now they meant to drive out these new English traders.

i18n.hi: जल्दी ही दक्षिण से पुर्तगाली पाल नजर आए। उनका इस्तादो इन समंदर राहों और जिद्दा जाने वाले हाजी जहाज़ों की रखवाली का दावा करता था; अब उनका इरादा इन नए अंग्रेज सौदागरों को भगा देने का था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mughal watchers on the beach, one noble shading his eyes, ships small but visible beyond the surf
panels.action: A Mughal noble on horseback shades his eyes with his hand, servants behind him; out past the surf, both English and Portuguese ships maneuver, their masts like thin dark needles against the sea.

dialogue.text: From the shore, the Mughal audience saw distant hulls turn and close, heard only the faint thud of guns. Yet on those movements, the future of Surat’s foreign merchants quietly swung.

i18n.hi: किनारे से मुगल दर्शक दूर के जहाज़ों को घूमते, भिड़ते देख पाए, बस तोपों की मंद धमक सुनाई दी। पर इन्हीं करवटों पर सूरत के परदेसियों की किस्मत टिकी थी।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-range sea-level shot between two English ships firing broadsides toward approaching Portuguese ships
panels.action: At sea level, an English ship heels as its cannon belch smoke toward oncoming Portuguese vessels; sailors strain at ropes while Best stands firm, silhouetted against the powder haze.

dialogue.text: Thomas Best’s own diary names the days and tides. In November and early December, his small squadron at Swally traded broadsides with the larger Portuguese force, fighting for command of the anchorage.

i18n.hi: थॉमस बेस्ट की डायरी दिन और ज्वारों का हिसाब देती है। नवंबर से शुरुआती दिसंबर तक, स्वाली पर उनकी छोटी टोली बड़े पुर्तगाली बेड़े से भिड़ती रही, लंगरगाह की बादशाही के लिए तोप-दर-तोप चलती रही।

panels.shot: close shot on Best on deck amid smoke, eyes intent, background of crew working the guns
panels.action: Through swirling gun smoke, Best grips the rail, jaw set, as crewmen run out another gun; the sea around them is choppy, dotted with bobbing debris.

dialogue.speaker: Thomas Best & Jahangir at Swally
dialogue.text: Stand to it, lads. Hold this road, and Surat must look our way.

i18n.hi: डटे रहो, जवानो। ये राह हमने थाम ली, तो सूरत को हमारी ओर ही देखना होगा।

panels.shot: wide aerial view of the battle thinning out, Portuguese ships turning away, English ships maintaining position off Suvali
panels.action: From above, Portuguese ships can be seen turning seaward, sails angled away from the anchorage, while the English vessels remain in formation closer to the shore of Suvali.

dialogue.text: The Portuguese did not destroy the English squadron or seize the anchorage. English guns held Swally’s waters, and the Mughal officials on shore saw which foreigners remained before Surat’s sea-gate.

i18n.hi: पुर्तगाली न अंग्रेज बेड़े को डुबा पाए, न लंगरगाह छीन पाए। अंग्रेज तोपों ने सुवाली का पानी थामे रखा, और किनारे के मुगल अमलों ने देख लिया कि सूरत के फाटक पर कौन-कौन ठहरे रह गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mughal noble dismounting and conferring with scribes and local intermediaries near the beach
panels.action: Near the dunes, a Mughal noble steps down from his horse, gesturing as he speaks with turbaned scribes and local brokers; one points alternately toward the English ships and inland toward Surat.

dialogue.text: The Mughals had watched two Christian powers test each other. Now came their part—not with muskets, but with ink and seals, choosing which flag might trade at their emperor’s port.

i18n.hi: मुगलों ने दो ईसाई ताकतों को एक-दूसरे को परखते देखा। अब उनकी बारी थी — न बंदूक से, बल्कि क़लम और मुहर से, कि किस झंडे को बादशाह के बंदर पर सौदा करने दिया जाए।

panels.shot: interior of a Surat house used as English factory, Best and factors seated with Mughal officials, documents between them
panels.action: Inside a modest but solid Surat house, Thomas Best and English factors sit respectfully on carpets opposite Mughal officials; between them lie folded Persian documents and small piles of coin and sample cloth.

dialogue.text: Best’s victory at Swally strengthened the English plea. With Portuguese ships kept at a distance, Mughal officers in Gujarat weighed the advantage of granting these newcomers a permanent trading house at Surat.

i18n.hi: स्वाली की जीत ने अंग्रेजों की दलील को जोर दिया। जब पुर्तगाली जहाज़ दूर रखे गए, गुजरात के मुगल अफसरों ने तौला कि सूरत में इन नए मेहमानों को पक्का कारखाना दे देना उनके हक में है या नहीं।

panels.shot: courtly interior shot in Jahangir’s presence, a vakil or ambassador bows while holding a Persian farman draft
panels.action: Back in an ornate hall, a courtly envoy bows before Jahangir, holding up a neatly written Persian scroll; nobles watch as the emperor listens, his face composed, a pen and inkwell set beside him.

dialogue.text: Jahangir later recorded how he granted the English leave to trade. In his memoir, it appears not as a thunderclap, but as one more royal decision—yet it rested on the outcome at distant Swally.

i18n.hi: जहांगीर ने बाद में लिखा कि उसने अंग्रेजों को सौदा करने की इजाज़त दी। उसकी यादों में ये कोई तड़की बिजली नहीं, बस एक और शाही फ़ैसला है — पर उसकी जड़ें दूर के सुवाली की जंग में थीं।

panels.shot: close shot of Jahangir’s hand signing or sealing a farman, with a faint hint of sea and ships painted on the wall behind
panels.action: A close view shows Jahangir’s ringed hand pressing a seal onto a folded farman, while in the blurred background a wall painting depicts ships on a tranquil sea.

dialogue.speaker: Thomas Best & Jahangir at Swally
dialogue.text: Let them dwell at Surat and bring profit; the port is ours, the sea is theirs.

i18n.hi: उन्हें सूरत में रहने दो, नफ़ा लाने दो; बंदर हमारा, समंदर उनका।

panels.shot: exterior shot of an early English factory building in Surat, with English and Indian merchants interacting
panels.action: Under the hot Gujarat sun, a plain but sturdy building near the river flies a small English flag; outside, English factors and Indian merchants confer over bales of cloth and chests, while porters move goods toward the water.

dialogue.text: The factory at Surat did not end Portuguese power, nor give the English an empire overnight. Yet it fixed them on India’s western shore, under Mughal protection, as one more player in the crowded trade.

i18n.hi: सूरत की फैक्टरी से न पुर्तगाली ताकत खत्म हुई, न अंग्रेजों को एक झटके में मुल्क मिल गया। पर इससे वे मुगल साये में हिंदुस्तान के पश्चिमी किनारे पर जड़ पकड़ बैठे — भीड़ भरे सौदे में एक और खिलाड़ी।

panels.shot: split composition showing, on one side, Portuguese ships still active elsewhere, and on the other, English ships loading at Surat
panels.action: On the left, Portuguese ships sail in another harbor with a fort onshore; on the right, English vessels are loaded at Surat’s anchorage, small boats ferrying goods, Mughal guards watching from the bank.

dialogue.text: Om Prakash and other historians note how Portuguese and English remained rivals for years. Swally gave the English local command of one anchorage and opened doors at court, but the wider contest went on.

i18n.hi: ओम प्रकाश जैसे इतिहासकार बताते हैं कि पुर्तगाली और अंग्रेज बरसों तक टक्कर में रहे। स्वाली ने बस एक लंगरगाह पर उन्हें बढ़त दी और दरबार के कुछ दरवाज़े खोले; बड़ी बाज़ी तो चलती ही रही।

panels.shot: concluding contemplative shot: wide view from above Swally beach, tiny English ships offshore, Mughal riders on the sand, sunset
panels.action: At sunset, tiny English ships lie offshore while a small group of Mughal horsemen ride slowly along the sandy Suvali beach, their shadows long on the ground, the river mouth and Surat beyond faint in the distance.

dialogue.text: Swally shows how an empire can be reshaped by battles it only watched—when Jahangir’s seal met Thomas Best’s guns, a new chapter of India’s sea-frontier quietly began at the edge of the surf.

i18n.hi: स्वाली दिखाता है कैसे कोई सल्तनत सिर्फ देखी हुई लड़ाइयों से भी बदल जाती है — जब जहांगीर की मुहर ने थॉमस बेस्ट की तोपों से हाथ मिलाया, हिंदुस्तान की समुंदरी सरहद पर लहरों के किनारे एक नया बाब खुल गया।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Distant Sea-Fight Opened the Gates of the Great Mughal’s Port
subtitle_i18n.hi: दूर के समुंदर की जंग ने मुगल बंदरगाह का फाटक कैसे खोला
